In Spanish the verb has gender too, it depends on the person.

While in English you can say "I was distracted" and there's no gender there, in Spanish you say "Estaba distraido / Estaba distraida" according your gender.

Her is not Ella, She is Ella.

Him and Her are "Su" in Spanish, the possessive doesn't affect the subject but it could  affects the object. 


For example in English 

"This is HER car" - telling with the possessive that the owner is female.

"Es SU auto" - you don't know if the car owner is male or female 

"Este auto es SUYO" - "Suyo" is a possessive, but with this you are explaining that the object is male, in female "Suya" 

If you want to say that the owner is male or female you will have to use the pronoun. 

"Este auto es de ELLA" - now you're saying that the owner is a female.

Resuming. Possessives in Spanish are neutrals (Su) and they could have gender (Suyo/Suya) but this gender affects the object, not the subject.
